question: Is the official vidore/colqwen2-v0.1 to vidore/colqwen2-v1.0 successor release a genuine decoder/projection update that preserves the post-vision replay boundary, rather than another convenience example selected after seeing tensor scope?

selection.reason: The source model card explicitly names v1.0 as its newer version; this named successor relation was frozen before tensor-header inspection.
selection.boundary: One additional official transition from the same publisher strengthens release-history characterization but is not a production-frequency sample.

competing_predictions.repeated_backend_update: Both checkpoints contain only decoder LoRA plus retrieval projection tensors under the same base and processor contract; post-vision replay is statically legal.
competing_predictions.publisher_label_is_misleading: The target checkpoint touches vision/base-embedding/unknown tensors or changes the processor/base contract; raw rebuild is required and the GPU experiment is cancelled.

gates.provenance: All frozen file hashes match the exact official revisions.
gates.changed_target: Source and target adapter checkpoint hashes differ.
gates.same_contract: Adapter config, base name, tensor key/shape contract, and processor bytes are identical.
gates.scope: Target has zero vision, base-embedding, and unknown tensors and at least one decoder plus one retrieval-projection tensor.
gates.gpu_promotion: Run the GPU canary only if every CPU gate passes.

claim_boundary: This is a deterministic inspection of one named official successor transition. It establishes dependency legality, not output correctness, retrieval quality, physical payoff, or deployment frequency.
